A1.justification: Both complete 61-page PDFs describe the same PENGUIN benchmark and RAISE framework. Text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison. Pages 11–61 are visually identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM evaluations, context-acquisition experiments and component comparisons in Sections 4–5, Table 2 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark evaluations, planning analyses and additional model results in the appendices.

M1.justification: RAISE retains the same offline LLM-guided MCTS planner and online retrieval, attribute-acquisition and abstention procedures. Section 5 and Algorithms 1–2 contain no procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14,000 PENGUIN scenarios across seven domains, equally divided between Reddit-derived and synthetic data, with the same context-free and context-rich evaluations.

E2.justification: The evaluated LLMs and Vanilla, +Agent and +Planner comparisons in Table 2 are unchanged. Attribute-selection comparators, abstention variants and the additional LLaMA-3-8B comparisons in Table 9 also remain identical.

E3.justification: The three-dimensional scoring framework, GPT-4o evaluation procedure, human-validation sample, acquisition budgets and model settings are unchanged. No evaluation protocol is added or revised in the appendices.

E4.justification: The attribute-sensitivity and subset-selection analyses, failure cases, MCTS convergence and stepwise-gain analyses, and abstention comparisons are retained unchanged in Sections 4.3–4.4 and Appendices B–D.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same correlation and evaluator-agreement analyses, including their significance reporting. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, GPT-4o's Table 2 averages remain 2.94, 3.66 and 3.83 for Vanilla, +Agent and +Planner, respectively.

T1.justification: The optimization and MDP formulations, search equations, and Appendix C.7 assumptions, convergence claims, bounds and proof sketches are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark and training-free RAISE contributions, including the reported 43.2% context benefit, 31.6% RAISE improvement and 2.7-query average.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning selective context acquisition and safety remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations of uniform attribute costs and manually defined attributes, along with the same appendix discussions and multimodal future-work directions.

D1.justification: The front-page project-homepage link is replaced by a direct Hugging Face link to wick1d/Personalized_Safety_Data, revising dataset-access information. Prompts, implementation settings, hardware descriptions and other reproducibility details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the reference list are unchanged. The paper retains the same positioning relative to prior LLM safety and personalization research.

P1.justification: The author block updates affiliation names and numbering, contact emails and punctuation, and removes the internship and corresponding-author footnotes. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged after matching text across page breaks.

P2.justification: The front-page author/link block and its small icon change, with consequent main-text reflow. Figures 4–5 move from page 7 to page 6; scientific graphics, captions and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 updates author information, substitutes a direct dataset link and modestly rearranges existing material. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, theory and limitations—including all appendices—remain unchanged. These limited editorial and access-information changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
